chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu al-Samit, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'A prayer in the Prophet's mosque (peace be upon him and his family) equals ten thousand prayers.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward multiplier for praying in the Prophet's mosque according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the unique spiritual merit of the Prophet's Mosque (Masjid al-Nabawi) in Medina, a status derived from the Prophet's own residence and burial place there. In Shia jurisprudence, this immense reward (thawab) distinguishes it from other mosques, though scholars note it does not necessarily imply exclusivity of validity, but rather superiority in reward. The narration reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the sanctity of the Ahl al-Bayt's physical spaces as conduits for divine grace.
